entries.algorithm_name: Distillation from Frontier Teachers (Llama 4 Behemoth → Scout/Maverick)
entries.eli5: Meta trained a 288B 'teacher' (Behemoth) that beats GPT-4.5, then distilled its knowledge into 17B-active 'students' (Scout, Maverick). Students get near-teacher quality at 1/10th the cost.
entries.purpose: Train a massive teacher model (frontier scale), then distill its capabilities into smaller, deployable student models via: (1) logit distillation, (2) synthetic data generation, (3) response imitation.
entries.input_dataset: Massive prompt dataset; teacher generates responses/logits for each.
usecase_scenarios: Llama 4 Behemoth (288B) → Scout (17B active) + Maverick (17B active)
entries.outcome: Small student models (17B active) that match models 5-10x their size on benchmarks; deployable on single GPU.
benchmark_metrics: Student quality at fixed param count

metadata.computational_complexity: Teacher: full frontier training cost. Student: ~10% of teacher training cost via distillation.
pros: Small deployable models with frontier quality
Teacher can be proprietary (only outputs shared)
Composable with all efficiency techniques (quant, sparse)
cons: Teacher biases/hallucinations propagate
Distillation data quality is critical
Capacity gap limits student quality
metadata.implementation_guide: (1) Train teacher at frontier scale (Llama 4 Behemoth: 288B active, 16 experts). (2) Generate massive prompt-response dataset with teacher. (3) Optionally include teacher logits for logit distillation. (4) SFT student on teacher outputs. (5) For best results: combine logit distillation (soft targets) + response SFT (hard targets) + RL on verifiable tasks (math, code). Llama 4 Scout/Maverick were distilled from Behemoth this way.
metadata.claude_specific_notes: Claude Haiku is distilled from Claude Opus/Sonnet. Llama 4 Behemoth → Scout/Maverick is the leading open example (Meta confirmed).
metadata.code_snippet:
# Distillation from frontier teacher (Llama 4 Behemoth-style)
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
def distill_from_teacher(student, teacher, prompts, alpha=0.5, T=2.0):
    for prompt in prompts:
        # Teacher generates response + logits (teacher in eval mode, no grad)
        with torch.no_grad():
            teacher_inputs = teacher.prepare(prompt)
            teacher_logits = teacher(teacher_inputs).logits / T
            teacher_probs = F.softmax(teacher_logits, dim=-1)
            # Optionally: teacher.generate() for sequence-level distillation
            teacher_response = teacher.generate(prompt)
        # Student forward
        student_inputs = student.prepare(prompt)
        student_logits = student(student_inputs).logits / T
        student_logprobs = F.log_softmax(student_logits, dim=-1)
        # KL divergence (soft) + cross-entropy on teacher's response (hard)
        soft_loss = F.kl_div(student_logprobs, teacher_probs, reduction='batchmean') * (T*T)
        hard_loss = F.cross_entropy(student_logits, teacher_response_ids)
        loss = alpha * soft_loss + (1 - alpha) * hard_loss
        loss.backward()

entries.algorithm_name: RL Infrastructure: Slime / veRL / OpenRLHF Comparison
entries.eli5: Three open-source frameworks for RL training of LLMs: Slime (Z.ai, used for GLM-4.5), veRL (VolcanoEngine), OpenRLHF. Each handles the complex dance of rollout+training+reward at scale.
entries.purpose: Provide open-source frameworks for RL training of LLMs (PPO, GRPO, RLAIF, agentic RL) with: rollout generation, reward computation, advantage estimation, policy update, all distributed across GPU clusters.
entries.input_dataset: RL training prompts + reward functions.
usecase_scenarios: DeepSeek-R1 (uses internal framework, similar to OpenRLHF)
Any team doing RL training of LLMs
entries.outcome: Production-grade RL training of LLMs at 70B-1T param scale.

metadata.computational_complexity: O(N_rollouts * rollout_len) + O(N_train_steps * model_FLOPs)
pros: Support both reasoning RL and agentic RL
cons: Each has different API (porting cost)
Async mode is complex to debug
Agentic RL with long rollouts needs careful tuning
metadata.implementation_guide: Choose based on needs: (1) Slime (Z.ai): best for agentic RL with long rollouts (disaggregated async mode). SGLang-native. (2) veRL (VolcanoEngine): good general-purpose, supports both sync and async. (3) OpenRLHF: most popular open-source, simpler. (4) NeMo-Aligner: NVIDIA-supported, integrates with Megatron. (5) TRL: easiest for small-scale experiments. For frontier-scale agentic RL, Slime is the leading choice (used for GLM-4.5).
